dedupe_keys.name: syntheticdhn realistic synthetic district heating network generator

description: SyntheticDHN is an open-source generator of synthetic third-generation district heating networks, developed in a PhD project by Dubon Rodrigue and co-authors at IMT Atlantique (Lab-STICC and GEPEA), who suggest it as a first step toward standard network benchmarks like the IEEE test cases for power systems. A constrained random graph model with the node method produces plausible layouts that reproduce properties of real networks such as degree distribution, maximum node degree and connectivity. Nodes become substations or junctions, and substations get synthetic year-long heating demand profiles derived from open data of the French agency ADEME. Outputs can feed node-based simulators such as HeatGrid. The method is location-independent, with demand profiles grounded in French data. It is Python code on GitHub, archived on Zenodo (updated October 2025), with code and data under the European Union Public Licence 1.2 at no cost, while the Zenodo archive lists CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: networks are synthetic and suit benchmarking, not representing any real system. Simulation uses are hydraulic and thermal network simulation and optimisation benchmarks. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
